09 SEP 2026NATIVE BELL PILOT VERIFIEDFULL ASSEMBLY PENDING
The bellmouth pilot is built and checked in nTop. The complete P5 recipe is prepared, but Windows locked before its native assembly run. This report distinguishes the actual pilot from the proposed casing and joint details. It is not a completed engine revision or a manufacturing release.

01 / INLETSpline profile, then Revolve

The new bell uses native cubic splines in the meridional plane. A closed wall profile is revolved 360 degrees about the engine axis. Tangent directions meet at the inner bell, rounded lip, and outer return.

FeatureP5 basisStatus
Bell lip envelope164 mm outer diameter; 8 mm lip radius.New study dimensions. Native pilot exported.
Main outer casing150 mm diameter, compared with 179 mm in P4.Proposed. Retained flange radius plus clearance and wall sets the diameter.
Compressor-side housing164 mm peak envelope near native Z = 45 mm.Proposed. Gives the front section fuller proportions.
Compressor rotor and diffuserRetain current native definitions.Larger housing is not a larger or rematched compressor.
Outer panel wallInward offset of the revolved outer solid, trimmed open at both ends.Prepared native construction. Full geometry must be checked.

The inlet curve changes the air-facing bell surface. The new outer casing surrounds the retained engine. These two changes do not establish improved inlet recovery or smoother flow through the compressor, diffuser, combustor, or turbine.

02 / ATTACHMENTHow the outer panels attach

P4 uses four screws on two internal split bands. They are hidden by the outer panels. The pressure casing has separate flange bolts. P4 did not define a qualified clamping or retention arrangement for the outer panels.

P5 proposes six support-ring halves at three stations. The existing inlet, case-split, and exhaust flange joints clamp those rings. Longer replacement flange screws accommodate the added ring thickness. Visible radial screws then attach each outer panel to the rings.

StationFlange attachmentVisible panel attachmentNominal stack
J01 / Inlet12 M4 x 20 screws, 12 nuts, 24 washers; two support-ring halves.6 M3 x 8 screws and washers at Z = 18.00 mm.12.0 mm grip; 3.2 mm thread protrusion.
J02 / Case12 M4 x 20 screws, 12 nuts, 24 washers; two support-ring halves.8 M3 x 8 screws and washers at Z = 151.50 mm.12.5 mm grip; 2.7 mm thread protrusion.
J03 / Exhaust12 M4 x 20 screws, 12 nuts, 24 washers; two support-ring halves.8 M3 x 8 screws and washers at Z = 224.69 mm.12.0 mm grip; 3.2 mm thread protrusion.

The front pattern omits two positions within the service opening. The proposed total is 22 panel screws and 22 washers. Thirty-six M4 x 20 flange screws replace the existing thirty-six M4 x 16 screws. Existing nuts and washers retain their dimensional envelopes.

Attachment path and assembly order

  1. Assemble the retained engine pressure casing and internal modules.
  2. Place the split support rings against the rear faces of the three flange joints. Install the longer flange screws, nuts, and washers.
  3. Fit the two removable panels to the cylindrical outer faces of the support rings.
  4. Install the radial panel screws through clearance holes into the ring receiver threads. Nominal engagement is 6 mm.

Panel loads pass through the radial screws and ring contact faces, then through the flange joints into the pressure casing. The outer fairing has no new hole through the pressure wall. Tool access, flange loads, preload, locking, thermal expansion, and thread strength still require verification.

04 / BASISDocumented assumptions

  1. The photo supplies styling and architecture clues only. It has no dimensional scale.
  2. The larger compressor section is interpreted as housing proportions. Retain the impeller and diffuser unless the user requests rotor redesign and engine rematching.
  3. The main nacelle radius is the retained 72 mm flange radius plus 1.5 mm radial clearance and 1.5 mm wall.
  4. Lip crown, lip radius, compressor bulge station and transition stations are unqualified design inputs.
  5. The bell uses cubic Bezier segments represented by native cubic splines. Offset ellipse axes approximate its wall; measure the resulting normal thickness.
  6. Three split support rings add 6 mm to the inlet, case-split and nozzle joint stacks. Replace their original M4 x 16 screws with M4 x 20 nominal envelopes.
  7. Twenty-two visible M3 radial screws attach the panels to threaded receiver envelopes. Six front screws avoid the service window; each other ring uses eight. Threads are envelopes.
  8. The rings contact the panels at the nominal radial interface and the existing flange rear faces. Loads, preload, locking, thread capacity, thermal movement and material compatibility remain unqualified.
  9. All original pressure-case and core expressions are retained. New visible hardware supersedes the three affected flange hardware groups.
  10. The outer nacelle is a ventilated fairing. Its access openings and seams are not pressure seals.
  11. An altered inlet shape does not validate pressure recovery, inlet distortion, compressor matching, thrust, life or manufacturing release.
